A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PARD research. All 15 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A, are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original inference benchmarks and ablations in Section 4, plus MI250X evaluation results in Appendix A, Table 7.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark, ablation, and cross-device results in Section 4 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Parallel drafting, mask-token training, shared mask-token IDs, and conditional token dropping are unchanged. Sections 3.1–3.2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same training corpora and the same mathematical reasoning and code-generation evaluations on MATH500, GSM8K, and HumanEval. No additional coverage appears in the appendix.

E2.justification: Comparator participation is unchanged throughout: AR, AR+, vanilla speculative decoding, and EAGLE remain in their respective comparisons. Appendix Table 7 retains AR Draft versus PARD.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, hardware, metrics, and decoding settings match. The 93K-sample ablation setup and vLLM evaluations across batch sizes 1–16 are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same conditional-drop sensitivity analysis, shared-versus-distinct mask-token comparison, training/inference draft-length analysis, acceptance-rate and bandwidth comparisons, batch-size analysis, and MI250X evaluation.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates and averages without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Section 1 changes the qualitative VSD-versus-EAGLE speedup finding from 'was lower' to 'may be lower,' withdrawing a definite ranking. All numerical results in Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–7, including Appendix A, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 retain the same objectives, probability factorizations, timing expressions, and token-retention derivation. Neither version contains additional appendix theory or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about parallel draft adaptation, target independence, conditional-drop training efficiency, and inference acceleration are unchanged in the abstract, contribution list, and conclusion.

C2.justification: The introduction qualifies the claimed consequence of greater draft-model computational cost: reduced speedup relative to EAGLE becomes a possibility rather than a definite consequence. Other mechanism explanations and applicability discussions are unchanged.

D1.justification: The v3 abstract newly states that code is available and supplies the AMD-AIG-AIMA/PARD repository address. v1 has no equivalent code-access information. Implementation and experimental details otherwise match.

R1.justification: The cited works and Section 5 are unchanged. PARD retains the same novelty and target-independence positioning relative to prior speculative-decoding approaches.

P1.justification: Localized edits correct 'Buajun Bai' to 'Huajun Bai,' add the abstract's code-access sentence, qualify the EAGLE comparison, and add a Figure 2 reference in Section 4.2. Section order and nearly all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded abstract produces small first-page spacing changes, and Table 1 shifts slightly within page 8. All six figures and seven tables retain their content, captions, and visual design.

improvement.justification: v3 adds a concrete code-access pointer absent from v1, corrects an author name, and makes the EAGLE speedup statement more cautious. These provide limited improvements in reproducibility information and precision. The methods, quantitative evidence, and appendix are unchanged; the linked code's contents cannot be assessed from the PDFs.
